title: lava config --json
description: Every config key the app resolved, flattened to dot notation, with the file that set it. The provenance is the point: 'where does this value come from?' is the question a config bug actually asks, and a bag of values cannot answer it. A key declared secret reports its value only under --reveal.

config.description: In file order: config/app.php first, then the rest alphabetically, each key in declaration order.

key.description: Dot path within the config bag, e.g. app.env.

value.description: The resolved value: any JSON, since a config file may hold an array. Null when this key's own name was redacted — reported by `secret`, never by an empty string that could be a real value. Inside an array value, a leaf whose own name looks secret is replaced by the redaction marker where it stood, so the rest of the structure stays readable.

from_file.description: The config file that set it, relative to the app root.

secret.description: True when this key's own NAME looked secret and --reveal was not passed, so `value` is null here. A leaf redacted inside an array value does not set this: the entry itself was not withheld, and the marker sits in `value` where the leaf was. Not a property of the key itself: the same key reports false under --reveal.
